description: Answer key for the weak sample project. Planted: target leakage (final_exam_score is a feature and passed = final_exam_score >= 50), report claims 5-fold CV but code uses one unseeded train_test_split, 97.8% claim not produced by the code (it prints 1.0 when the path is fixed), fabricated reference (Johnson & Patel 2021, DOI 10.9999/... does not resolve), real reference cited for an unrelated claim (Breiman 2001 for a sleep/exam claim), no baseline, accuracy only on a 74/26 imbalanced target, no literature review, no limitations, hardcoded absolute path, no requirements.txt, no seed, no run instructions. The leakage is NOT detected by the deterministic scanner: only a reviewer that reads the code and data catches it.

expected_findings.label: problem definition / research question
expected_findings.why: Goal stated ('predict if a student will pass'), but no research question or hypothesis.

expected_findings.label: measurable objective
expected_findings.why: No target metric or success threshold defined up front.

expected_findings.label: inputs/outputs, why ML
expected_findings.why: 'AI is changing the world' is not a justification.

expected_findings.label: limitations
expected_findings.why: No scope, assumptions or limitations section.

expected_findings.label: literature review
expected_findings.why: No related-work section; two citations used as decoration.

expected_findings.label: recent literature
expected_findings.why: The only 'recent' reference is fabricated.

expected_findings.label: unverifiable / unsupporting citation
expected_findings.why: Johnson & Patel (2021) does not exist (DOI unresolvable). Breiman (2001) is real but says nothing about sleep and exams.

expected_findings.label: research gap
expected_findings.why: None.

expected_findings.label: dataset source and license
expected_findings.why: No source, license or collection description.

expected_findings.label: dataset explanation
expected_findings.why: Columns listed, but no size or class distribution, and final_exam_score is not even mentioned.

expected_findings.label: data quality
expected_findings.why: 'Rows with missing values were removed' (8 of 240) without analysis.

expected_findings.label: target leakage
expected_findings.why: model.py L13 adds final_exam_score as a feature; passed is a threshold of that score.

expected_findings.label: bias / dataset limitations
expected_findings.why: Not discussed despite the proposal to use the model on real students.

expected_findings.label: baseline model
expected_findings.why: Only a Random Forest; no majority or simple baseline.

expected_findings.label: model choice justified
expected_findings.why: 'Powerful model' and a fabricated citation.

expected_findings.label: train/test explanation
expected_findings.why: Split, preprocessing and training procedure are not described (and the described CV does not exist).

expected_findings.label: hyperparameters
expected_findings.why: n_estimators=100 in code but not documented; no tuning rationale.

expected_findings.label: basic ML model exists
expected_findings.why: model.py trains and evaluates a classifier (runs once the path is fixed); a single flat script, so PARTIAL is also defensible.

expected_findings.label: report/code inconsistency (CV)
expected_findings.why: report.md Method claims 5-fold cross-validation; model.py L16-20 is a single train_test_split.

expected_findings.label: hardcoded dataset path
expected_findings.why: model.py L7 absolute path C:/Users/student/Desktop/...

expected_findings.label: code quality
expected_findings.why: Flat script, no functions, no tests, chained assignment on a slice.

expected_findings.label: comparison with baseline
expected_findings.why: Nothing to compare against.

expected_findings.label: variability / significance
expected_findings.why: Single unseeded split.

expected_findings.label: ablation
expected_findings.why: Single-model approach.

expected_findings.label: unsupported result claims
expected_findings.why: 97.8% (5-fold CV) and 'better than other approaches' are not produced or supported by any code or output.

expected_findings.label: only accuracy reported
expected_findings.why: Accuracy only, unjustified, on a 74/26 imbalanced target; no precision/recall/F1.

expected_findings.label: error analysis
expected_findings.why: No confusion matrix or failure analysis.

expected_findings.label: generalization
expected_findings.why: No train vs test comparison.

expected_findings.label: missing requirements.txt
expected_findings.why: No dependency file.

expected_findings.label: no random seed
expected_findings.why: No random_state on split or model.

expected_findings.label: no reproducibility instructions
expected_findings.why: README has no run instructions; path breaks the script on any other machine.

expected_findings.label: results traceable
expected_findings.why: No saved outputs; the code prints a number that differs from the report.

expected_findings.label: poor README
expected_findings.why: Three sentences and a file list; no setup or run steps.

expected_findings.label: report structure
expected_findings.why: Has headings but no related work, results table, discussion or limitations.

expected_findings.label: ethics
expected_findings.why: Proposes flagging real students without any ethics discussion.

expected_findings.label: presentation
expected_findings.why: No slides.

expected_findings.label: figures/tables
expected_findings.why: No figures or tables; the single reported number does not match the code.
